articles.title: 'Big Bang' Fix Puts Voyager Across the 'One Light-Day' Mark
articles.description: Flashback to 1977. Jimmy Carter was U.S. president, Star Wars was a box office hit, and the two Voyager spacecraft departed on an historic Grand Tour of the solar system. Now, teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory are working to keep the missions active, as they push the boundaries of interstellar space beyond the solar system.
articles.summary: Voyager spacecraft reach the historic one light-day milestone from Earth, marking nearly 50 years of groundbreaking interstellar exploration.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft has captured the first clear images of the asteroids involved in NASA's groundbreaking 2022 DART impact experiment, revealing the aftermath of humanity's first planetary defense test.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have made a breakthrough discovery of evidence for an extraordinarily rare particle decay after a 42-year search, opening new windows into fundamental physics.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers have observed two different kinds of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart, an unprecedented cosmic event never witnessed before. Gamma-ray bursts are among the most energetic phenomena in the universe since the Big Bang.

articles.title: NASA Announces $1 Million to Students for Moon Base Challenge
articles.description: On Sunday, NASA announced the opening of its $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge during a MAX POWER event at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida. As part of a Golden Age of Science, the competition invites student teams at U.S. high schools and post-secondary schools to contribute designs for the Moon Base. “We’re […]
articles.summary: NASA announces a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to inspire the next generation of space explorers and engineers.

articles.title: NASA Awards Moon Base Transportation, Technology, Science Projects
articles.description: NASA announced a suite of awards and mission updates on Saturday to expand the agency’s Moon Base exploration, science, and infrastructure capabilities. The investments will advance commercial robotic deliveries, a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE, launch and orbital transfer services, and surface infrastructure as the agency works with American industry to establish a sustained presence on […]
articles.summary: NASA awards funding for Moon Base transportation, technology, and science projects to accelerate lunar exploration capabilities.

articles.title: NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps
articles.description: NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation […]
articles.summary: NASA opens applications for its Astronaut Corps, recruiting the next generation of space explorers for future human spaceflight missions.

articles.title: The ELT Can Probe Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies and Their Dark Matter Mysteries
articles.description: Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies are strange because they're as large as the Milky Way, but have far fewer stars. It's as if they're puffed up for some reason. Determining what's going on with them could help confirm the Lambda-CDM model. A new proposed instrument for the Extremely Large Telescope could give astronomers their best look yet at these strange galaxies.
articles.summary: The Extremely Large Telescope opens new possibilities for studying ultra-diffuse galaxies and unraveling the mysteries of dark matter distribution.

articles.title: NASA's Twin Spacecraft Will Execute Powered Slingshot Maneuvers on Their Way to Mars
articles.description: NASA's ESCAPADE mission features a pair of identical spacecraft on their way to Mars. They launched outside of the normal launch window, so they'll perform powered slingshot maneuvers to boost their speed. Once there, they'll "fly" in formation and study how the solar wind interacts with what remains of Mars ancient magnetosphere.
articles.summary: NASA's ESCAPADE mission deploys twin spacecraft performing innovative powered slingshot maneuvers en route to Mars exploration.

articles.title: A Mighty Wind Blew Away Gas and Made Early Galaxies Brighter
articles.description: When astronomers looked at photos of the early universe taken by the James Webb Space Telescope, they found something odd: an overabundance of bright galaxies about 400 to 500 million years after the Big Bang. But these galaxies should have been far less common so soon after the Big Bang. Researchers may have figured this out: Powerful ultraviolet (Lyman-alpha) radiation produced by dense clusters of young stars acted like a leaf blower, driving light-blocking gas and dust out of the galaxy and thereby making the galaxies appear brighter.
articles.summary: James Webb Space Telescope observations reveal that powerful cosmic winds stripped gas from early galaxies, making them brighter and more luminous.

articles.title: Interstellar Visitor 3I/ATLAS Shows Water Ice Behaves the Same Across Alien Star Systems
articles.description: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. And it just so happens that in the intervening years between the last known interstellar visitor (2I/Borisov in 2019), we got a major upgrade in our observational capabilities with the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). A new paper from a team of researchers led by Dr. Silvia Protopapa of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the Southwest Research Institute, and published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, details JWST’s findings on the water ice content of this most recent visitor from beyond our solar system.
articles.summary: Scientists studying the interstellar visitor 3I/ATLAS discovered that water ice behaves consistently across different star systems, providing insights into the composition of objects from beyond our solar system.

articles.title: JWST tracks more than 100 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy
articles.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a team of astronomers identified 104 magnified stellar events in a galaxy known as the Dragon, located around 6.5 billion light-years away. This discovery more than doubles the previous record of 44 such detections in the same galaxy. Because these kinds of events reveal some of the most luminous stars and likely the presence of dark matter, this study offers a rare look at the galaxy's stellar population along with a possible hint at the nature of dark matter.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope identified over 100 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy, advancing our understanding of stellar phenomena in distant galaxies.

articles.title: Want to fly to the moon? NASA is looking for new astronauts to help grow its Artemis program
articles.description: Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base? NASA is accepting applications for a new astronaut class that will help grow the Artemis program.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA is recruiting new astronauts to join the Artemis program and help establish a permanent human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
articles.description: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," is published in the journal Universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: An alternative cosmological model proposing a 26.7 billion-year-old universe without dark matter or dark energy has successfully passed key observational tests.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: Recent observations of mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may still possess active geological processes, challenging previous assumptions about the planet's dormancy.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
articles.description: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky. The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy 355,000 light-years away and a star cluster hidden behind cosmic dust. Scientists suspect hundreds of additional satellite galaxies remain undiscovered, and Rubin's powerful telescope could finally bring them into view.
articles.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has discovered two previously unknown satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, with the potential to find hundreds more previously hidden companions.

articles.title: A dead star's mysterious rings reveal what could happen when our Sun dies
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered a strange double ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star, revealing a possible preview of our Solar System's distant future. The two rings are separated by a mysterious gap that researchers believe is maintained by surviving planetary bodies, including one potentially as large as Pluto or the Moon. Their different chemical compositions suggest they may contain the remains of separate destroyed planets.
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a mysterious double ring of planetary debris orbiting a dead star, offering a fascinating glimpse into what may occur when our Sun reaches the end of its life.

articles.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
articles.description: By modeling how a planet without life develops its atmosphere, astronomers hope to be able to better distinguish rocky planets without life from those that are inhabited.
articles.summary: Scientists have developed atmospheric simulations of lifeless planets to better identify biosignatures and distinguish potentially habitable worlds in the search for extraterrestrial life.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.description: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission, the first Mars mission in 20 years. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: NASA's Mars Global Surveyor, launched November 7, 1992, was the agency's first Mars mission in two decades and provided unprecedented mapping of the Red Planet's surface.

articles.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
articles.description: NASA is asking the public to send their names to Titan for an ambitious mission that will see a flying craft explore the Saturn moon in 2034, if all goes according to plan.
articles.summary: NASA invites the public to send their names aboard the upcoming Dragonfly mission, which will explore Saturn's moon Titan with an innovative flying rotorcraft.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists using the Large Hadron Collider have peered into the subatomic zeptoverse to search for exotic particles and advance our understanding of fundamental matter.

articles.summary: Researchers have used nanohertz gravitational wave observations to constrain the properties of supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn, revealing insights into the early universe.

articles.title: In 1901, sponge divers off the Greek island of Antikythera recovered a corroded lump of bronze from a 2,000-year-old shipwreck; scans later showed it was a geared device built to predict eclipses
articles.description: In 1900, a remarkable discovery was made when divers stumbled upon the Antikythera Mechanism amidst a shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea. This ancient artifact showcased astounding knowledge of astronomy and mechanical engineering dating back over 2,000 years…
articles.summary: The ancient Antikythera Mechanism, recovered from a 2,000-year-old Greek shipwreck, was revealed through modern scans to be a sophisticated geared device designed to predict eclipses. This remarkable artifact demonstrates the advanced astronomical knowledge of the ancient world.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Discovered the 6th Dwarf Planet
articles.description: The other five are Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
articles.summary: Researchers may have discovered a sixth dwarf planet in our solar system, joining the known five: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake. This finding expands our understanding of small bodies in the outer solar system.

articles.summary: The ESA's Hera probe has reached an asteroid system that was previously impacted by NASA as part of planetary defense testing. This follow-up mission will study the effects of the impact and advance humanity's ability to protect Earth from asteroid threats.

articles.title: Trump's makes nuclear push in space exploration, sets 2-yr deadline for Nasa's Mars mission
articles.description: NASA is gearing up to launch an innovative nuclear-powered spacecraft towards Mars within the next two years. This ambitious mission is set to pioneer advanced nuclear-electric propulsion technology, critical for future exploration efforts. With a focus on re…
articles.summary: NASA is developing an innovative nuclear-powered spacecraft for Mars exploration with ambitious mission timelines. This advanced propulsion technology represents a major step forward in enabling human missions to the Red Planet.

articles.description: SpaceX vise le 13 novembre pour le quinzième vol d'essai intégré de Starship, au cours duquel l'entreprise tentera de rattraper à la fois le booster Super Heavy et l'étage supérieur à l'aide de la tour de lancement de Starbase. Si elle réussit, cette double c…
articles.summary: SpaceX is planning to attempt catching the Starship with giant mechanical arms during its 15th integrated flight test on November 13, marking a spectacular and ambitious milestone in reusable rocket technology. This maneuver represents an innovative approach to spacecraft recovery and reusability.
